data.title: Tombill Mines names new CFO
data.description:
• Tombill Mines (TBLL:CA) said on Friday that it has appointed Ashley Nadon as its new chief financial officer.
  • She will succeed Athanasios Pythagoras, who will work alongside Nadon during the transition.
  • Nadon is a chartered professional accountant with extensive experience providing financial management, accounting, and regulatory compliance services to publicly traded companies.
  • She currently serves as CFO for several TSX Venture Exchange-listed junior resource exploration companies.
  • Press Release

data.title: Verizon in talks to buy Fidium in $6B deal — FT
data.description:
Verizon (VZ) is in discussions to purchase fibre-optic broadband operator Fidium for about $6 billion.

Talks between Verizon and Fidium’s owners, Searchlight Capital Partners, and Canadian fund manager British Columbia Investment Management Corporation are ongoing, according to a Financial Times report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. A potential $6 billion deal, which includes debt, could happen in the coming weeks. 

It's possible that another bidder could emerge, and there are no guarantees the talks will result in a transaction, according to the report. Searchlight and BCI bought Fidium, then known as Consolidated Communications, in a $3.1 billion take-private deal in 2024.

Verizon and Searchlight declined to comment to the FT. BCI and Fidium did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

data.title: Advantage Energy holder to vote against sale to Canadian Natural Resources
data.description:
Andvantage Energy (AAVVF) holder LetkoBrosseau said it plans to vote against its  sale to Canadian Natural Resources (CNQ) and urges fellow holders to reject the offer.

LetkoBrosseau, which has a 5.5% stake in Advantage Energy (AAVVF), is against the deal, as it “significantly undervalues” the company's "high-quality" asset base and long-term potential, according to a statement on Friday.

"CNQ's proposal represents highly opportunistic timing designed to acquire premier, long-life assets at the bottom of the natural gas cycle and during a period of leadership transition,"  LetkoBrosseau said in the statement. "But given Advantage's leading asset base and strong financial position, it should feel no pressure to pursue a deal now. In fact, when further considering the industry's accelerating M&A environment, the company actually possesses an enviable negotiating position; it is thus weakly playing what is in reality a very good hand."

The comments come after Canadian Natural (CNQ) last Monday said it agreed to acquire Advantage Energy (AAVVF) for ~C$2.53 (US$1.77B), including debt, bolstering the company's position in western Canada. Canadian Natural (CNQ) said it will pay C$13.55/share for Advantage (AAVVF), a nearly 20% premium.

data.title: Valero breaks losing streak, but 'hold rating' and $300 warning loom
data.description:
Valero Energy (VLO) shares broke a week-long losing streak on Friday, November 27, rising ~2% to ~$329.37 after falling from ~$344 on November 20 to an intraday low near $314 on Wednesday.

Despite the recent pullback, Valero Energy has sharply outperformed the broader market this year. The stock has gained 101.81% year-to-date, compared with a 4.93% return for the S&P 500 (SP500).

According to the five-minute TradingView chart, the stock recovered above its 50-, 100-, and 200-period simple moving averages during Friday's surge. These averages now sit below the share price, at $327.14, $323.85, and $325.05, respectively, providing potential short-term support.

According to the technical indicators, momentum also points to improving near-term sentiment. The 14-period RSI stood at 56.24, in neutral territory, while the MACD lines remained above zero. 

The slight Valero Energy stock rebound comes as analysts remain divided on its outlook. Seeking Alpha analysts and Wall Street maintain Hold ratings, with scores of 3.00 and 3.40, respectively. Seeking Alpha's Quant system, meanwhile, rates the stock Strong Buy with a score of 4.98.

In a recent bearish assessment, Seeking Alpha analyst Seeking Profits downgraded Valero Energy to Sell and placed a fair value near $300, implying roughly 9% downside from today's $329.37 level.

The analyst argued that investors may be overestimating the benefits of elevated refining margins driven by geopolitical disruptions.

For now, today's rebound pushed Valero Energy back above all three key moving averages, placing the $323.85–$327.14 range as a potential support zone. Holding above this area could help sustain the recovery, while a drop below it may weaken the improving short-term outlook.

data.title: Jazz wins approval of Ziihera for gastroesophageal cancer in UK
data.description:
• The UK's Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has approved Jazz Pharmaceuticals' (JAZZ) Ziihera (zanidatamab ) for gastroesophageal cancer.
  • The indication is for individuals whose cancer has high levels of the protein HER2. 
  • Ziihera was already indicated for bile duct cancer. 
  • Approval was based on a study of HER2+ gastroesophageal cancer patients. Those who received Ziihera plus BeOne Medicines' (ONC) Tevimbra (tislelizumab) and chemotherapy had longer overall survival and better progression-free survival compared to those who received just Herceptin and chemo.

data.title: Stocks hit the sales early: S&P 500 up 1.5% on Black Friday
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) was on track for one of its strongest Black Friday performances on record, rising 1.1% in morning trading, according to data shared by Ryan Detrick of Carson Investment Research.

“Two hours to go, but this is currently one of the better Black Friday returns ever for the S&P 500,” Detrick wrote on X.

Data posted by Detrick showed the S&P 500's strongest Black Friday gains included a 1.8% rise in 1971, a 1.7% advance in 2007, and gains of 1.5% in both 1984 and 2000. The index also rose 1.4% in 1963 and 1.3% in 2012.

The 2026 advance was among 12 Black Friday sessions since 1950 in which the index gained more than 1%. Its 1.1% rise was in line with gains recorded in 1956, 1957, and 1958. The 2026 figure is based on the index's intraday price and does not represent its final closing return.

At the time of writing, the blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last +1.2%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +1.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last +2%.

data.title: Dutch drugmaker Lundbeck reportedly eyeing deals in psychedelic space
data.description:
Companies focused on psychedelic medicines traded higher on Friday after The Wall Street Journal reported that Dutch drugmaker Lundbeck (HLBBF) (HLUBF) is exploring deals in that space.

Notable gainers include Helus Pharma (HELP), Compass Pathways (CMPS), Definium Therapeutics (DFTX), GH Research (GHRS), and Bright Minds Biosciences (DRUG).

“We are mapping the space, and we have quite active conversations around what is happening in this landscape,” Lundbeck (HLUBF) CEO Charl van Zyl said during an interview. “There are some more late-stage companies, and then there are also obviously more early-stage-profiled companies. We keep looking at all these options,” he added.

His remarks came amid growing interest in psychedelic space among big pharma following a series of favorable regulatory measures under the Trump administration.

Earlier this year, President Donald Trump issued an executive order to speed up research into psychedelic-based drugs, a move aimed at making substances such as psilocybin, LSD, and MDMA widely available in the U.S.

In September, Eli Lilly (LLY) acquired psychedelic drugmaker AtaiBeckley for more than $2.8B. “We also like that space,” van Zyl said. “We think it’s got a lot of clinical relevance, and the body of evidence has increased a lot, so we continue to look in that space.”

Known for antidepressants such as citalopram and escitalopram, Lundbeck (HLUBF) has shifted its focus away from psychiatric therapies to rare neurological diseases and migraine in recent years. One of its most advanced candidates includes a rare epilepsy treatment called bexicaserin, which it added in 2024 from its $2.6B acquisition of U.S.-based Longboard Pharma.

Lundbeck's (HLUBF) strategy is not solely reliant on M&A, according to van Zyl, who added that the company is also seeking deals to strengthen its product pipeline.

“As they say, we continue to shop even if we’re not hungry,” Van Zyl said. “We continue to look for things that will allow us to bolster where we have know-how and where we have expertise.”

data.title: Midday Need to Know: Brazil stocks surge, SK Hynix boosts buybacks & more
data.description:
Wall Street climbed higher on Black Friday as major indices posted gains following the shortened Thanksgiving holiday week, with traders reassessing positions amid lighter trading volumes.

Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:

US goods trade deficit widens: The U.S. international trade in goods deficit  expanded to $149.5 billion in October, up from $135.1 billion in September and well above the -$133.0 billion consensus estimate. Imports surged $21.1 billion to $365.3 billion, while exports rose $6.7 billion to $215.8 billion. Wholesale inventories climbed 0.9% to $1,023.4 billion, with durable goods inventory growth accelerating to 1.6% month-over-month from 0.6% in September.

Brazilian stocks surge on finance minister pick: Brazil's benchmark Ibovespa index  jumped 2.6% to hover above 181.5K on Friday, extending a 6.1% rally from the prior session after Bradesco board chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco was confirmed as finance minister. The Planalto Palace announced Thursday night that Trabuco had accepted President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's invitation. Investors view the banking executive as likely to curb public spending, easing fiscal concerns that have pressured Brazilian equities amid elevated domestic yields since Lula's re-election. Bradesco shares soared 17%, XP gained 18%, and Itaú Unibanco rose 13%.

SK Hynix accelerates share repurchases: SK Hynix  doubled its daily share buyback volume to 700,000 shares from 350,000 on Friday, citing concerns that its stock has become undervalued following a broader semiconductor market sell-off. The memory maker's Nasdaq-listed ADRs rose nearly 4% in limited Friday trading. After its June IPO at $149 per ADR, shares peaked at $198 in September but have declined steadily since October. The company also disclosed plans to deliver 100 trillion won in shareholder returns in fiscal 2026, including at least 30 trillion won in cash dividends.

US Air Force Cloud One system breached: Hackers  reportedly breached the U.S. Air Force's flagship Cloud One computing platform, potentially jeopardizing sensitive tactical, personnel, and logistics data. The intrusion was discovered within the past month during system upgrade work and has led to widespread disruption across the platform. Efforts to migrate back-office applications to Cloud One have been paused, software updates were blocked, and some users had administrator rights revoked. Investigators have called in Cyber Command to assess the damage. Cloud One combines resources from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, and Alphabet to power scores of Air Force applications.

data.title: AI shopping gains ground as Salesforce sees Black Friday sales hitting $83B
data.description:
Black Friday is on track to remain the biggest shopping day of the year, with global online sales expected to reach $83 billion, while artificial intelligence is playing an increasingly prominent role in how consumers find and buy products.

Salesforce (CRM) expects worldwide online spending to rise 5% year over year, with U.S. sales reaching $18.7 billion, up 4%. The forecast follows a record Thanksgiving, when online purchases totaled $37.2 billion globally, up 4.6%, including $8.8 billion in the U.S.

AI is becoming a bigger part of that shopping activity. Nearly one-quarter of holiday orders so far have been influenced by AI, while referral traffic from AI agent channels jumped 75% from a year earlier. One in five shoppers now starts their shopping journey with an AI tool.

Retailers could also be seeing bigger orders from shoppers using their AI assistants. Consumers who interacted with a brand-owned shopping agent on Thanksgiving spent 43% more per order than those who did not.

The AI landscape is shifting, too. Gemini (GOOG) has overtaken ChatGPT (OPENAI) in global traffic share, although ChatGPT remains the leading AI channel in the U.S.

Social shopping also gained ground, with TikTok Shop (TIKTOK) orders surging 332% year over year on Thanksgiving. Social media accounted for 23% of global ecommerce traffic, up 18%, while the share of orders originating from social referrals climbed 34% to 6.3%.

Appliances were the fastest-growing global shopping category, with online sales rising 27%, followed by active footwear and active apparel. In the U.S., active apparel and footwear led category growth at 21%, while home sales increased 19%.

Meanwhile, bots and crawlers accounted for 30% of Thanksgiving ecommerce traffic. Mobile devices generated 82% of global online traffic and 73% of orders.
